01 Antidepressants · class card

MAOIs

monoamine oxidase inhibitors · phenelzine · tranylcypromine · isocarboxazid · selegiline patch

Practice
  1. 41-year-old man with depression unresponsive to four antidepressant trials now on fluoxetine; his psychiatrist plans tranylcypromine no psychotic features, no suicidal ideation asks when the new drug can start BP 124/80 mm Hg · HR 72/min → Stop fluoxetine, wait 5 weeks, then start → fluoxetine has a long half-life, so 5 weeks must pass before an MAOI; at least 2 weeks must pass after other serotonergic drugs, and any overlap risks serotonin syndrome
  2. 48-year-old woman on phenelzine at a wine-and-cheese party sudden blurred vision and drenching sweat no new medicines; no tremor or clonus BP 228/124 mm Hg · HR 112/min · T 37.1 °C → Phentolamine → wine and aged cheese on an MAOI bring a tyramine hypertensive crisis, treated with phentolamine; cyproheptadine is for serotonin syndrome, and physostigmine for severe anticholinergic toxicity with hot, dry skin
  3. 56-year-old man on phenelzine given meperidine after knee surgery 3 hours later agitated, sweating and shivering hyperreflexia; clonus at both ankles T 39.4 °C · BP 168/96 mm Hg · HR 124/min → Serotonin syndrome → meperidine is contraindicated with an MAOI because the pair causes serotonin syndrome, typically fever, autonomic instability, hyperreflexia and clonus; the tyramine crisis follows aged food or a sympathomimetic, and anticholinergic toxicity leaves the skin dry
